    Mesh corrections on a connected periodic quiver in characteristic two #

    characteristic-two-mesh-calculations.tex: "We will show that each periodic component contributes at most one correction line, represented by a single path." On a finite connected stable translation quiver with a finite-dimensional scalar mesh category satisfying the brick hypothesis, in characteristic two, the cokernels of the mesh derivatives are spanned by the class of at most one row (connected_cokerSpan): by Proposition 4.1 the quiver is covered by a star model; the types A give zero cokernels, and the types D, E one row of degree 2s + 2 at the centre.

    source
    def MultiplicativeBasisDeformations.StarTrace.DEModel {V : Type v'} [Quiver V] {Q : TranslationQuiver V} (hQ : Q.IsStable) (R : (x : ↑Q.nonprojective) × Quiver.Path ↑(Q.tau x) ↑x) :
    Prop

    The model of a row of type D or E (Proposition 6.1(1)(2)): the quiver is ℤΔ/⟨g⟩ for a three-arm Dynkin star Δ, with g(v, j) = (ρ v, j + 2s) (that is, τ^{−s} ρ), ρ an automorphism of Δ fixing the centre, s ≥ 1, and the row has degree 2s + 2.
